claims.claim: Modern improvements in labor tools, such as mute robots, have made the effort of sustaining life and giving birth easier, but they have not eliminated compulsion or human subjection to necessity.
qualifications: has made labor easier and less painful
has not eliminated compulsion or the condition of being subject to need and necessity
claims.supporting_excerpt: It is true that the enormous improvement in our labor tools—the mute robots with which homo faber has come to the help of the animal laborans , as distinguished from the human, speaking instruments (the instrumentum vocale , as the slaves in ancient households were called) whom the man of action had to rule and oppress when he wanted to liberate the animal laborans from its bondage—has made the twofold labor of life, the effort of its sustenance and the pain of giving birth, easier and less painful than it has ever been. This, of course, has not eliminated compulsion from the laboring activity or the condition of being subject to need and necessity from human life.

claims.claim: Tools and instruments are products of work rather than labor, and while they can ease labor and multiply human strength, no work can be produced without tools.
qualifications: not a product of labor but of work
birth of homo faber and the coming into being of a man-made world of things are coeval with the discovery of tools and instruments
claims.supporting_excerpt: Tools and instruments which can ease the effort of labor considerably are themselves not a product of labor but of work; they do not belong in the process of consumption but are part and parcel of the world of use objects. Their role, no matter how great it may be in the labor of any given civilization, can never attain the fundamental importance of tools for all kinds of work. No work can be produced without tools, and the birth of homo faber and the coming into being of a man-made world of things are actually coeval with the discovery of tools and instruments.

definitions.definition: The human condition or aspect focused on the endless cycle of biological life and labor, requiring sustenance and service.
The maker or fabricator of the man-made world of things, whose activities result in tools, instruments, and use objects.
Living, speaking instruments, historically referring to slaves in ancient households who served the living process rather than producing durable works.

distinctions.distinction: Tools of workmanship result in something more than the mere use of the instrument and have a controllable end in a finished product, whereas household instruments are tied to the endless, consuming process of living.
distinctions.item_b: Instruments of the household / living service

must_not_be_lost: Freedom requires knowing that one is subject to necessity.
Household slaves in antiquity were instruments of living rather than instruments of making things or production.
The endless process of life requires a perpetuum mobile or a living organism to serve it, which inanimate tools and gadgets cannot fully replace.
output.segment_function: The author analyzes the distinction and relationship between labor tools and work instruments, contrasting modern robotic assistance with ancient slavery, and explaining why tools of production can never fully replace the living service required by the endless biological process of life.
